decisions.reason: As the broader dietary-supplement range is close to the firm's established consumer-health business and received dedicated website support, a large firm with some slack would likely keep it unless performance clearly fell below aspiration.
The skin-and-hair supplement is in a crowded and easily substitutable niche, so if results were even modestly below aspiration management would be relatively likely to redeploy resources elsewhere.

A joint-health supplement fits pharmacy channels and the firm's existing portfolio well, so boundedly rational management would likely continue it while evidence remains mixed rather than terminate it quickly.
The immune-support supplement had visible launch backing and likely benefited from stronger category demand, making it more likely to stay above aspiration and be retained.

The generic blood-pressure medicine uses the firm's manufacturing, quality, and regulatory capabilities and supports relationships with pharmacies and insurers, so it is more likely to be kept unless margins disappoint sharply.

The OTC migraine triptan is somewhat more exploratory for the firm, but it still fits the pharmacy OTC strategy and a large established company would often keep such a product a bit longer while learning its market potential.
